observation.visible_scene: A calm lake at dawn/dusk viewed from the bow of a small boat (dark boat prow silhouetted across the bottom). On the right, a cluster of tall pine trees forms a dark island silhouette reflected in the still water; on the left horizon a low forest line glows against an orange-to-blue sky streaked with pink contrails. A thin layer of mist drifts just above the water. In the middle distance sit a floating dock with a small ladder and, further left, a low boat-like silhouette. In the near water, concentric ripples spread from a small disturbance point beside a few emergent reed stalks.
visible_changes: The circular ripple rings in the foreground water continuously expand outward from their source point near the reeds, growing larger and fainter as the clip progresses (expansion of the pattern, not lateral translation of the rings).

The dark tree-island reflection and the dock/boat reflections shimmer and deform slightly as the water surface moves, but the silhouetted objects themselves (dock, left boat, pines, tree line, contrails) keep fixed positions in the frame.
The foreground boat bow and the overall framing stay essentially fixed, indicating no deliberate pan or zoom; only the water and its reflections change.
Mist over the water remains present and largely steady throughout, with no clear directional drift visible in this short window.
outside_clip_unknowns: What created the ripple source (a fish, insect, dropped object, etc.) is not shown; the disturbance is already underway at the first frame.
Whether the ripples fully dissipate after the clip ends is unknown; they are still visible at the last frame.
Any earlier or later change in sky color, mist density, or water state is outside this segment.
uncertain_details: Possible very slight camera bob from the boat is indistinguishable from water-surface motion; no confident camera translation is supported.
The exact center of the ripple source is partly obscured by reeds and reflections, so its precise origin point is approximate.
